characters.name: Ebenezer Scrooge
characters.notes: Miserly partner; protagonist whose reclamation drives the story

characters.name: Jacob Marley
characters.notes: Dead partner; appears as chained ghost to warn Scrooge

characters.name: Bob Cratchit
characters.notes: Underpaid clerk with large poor family; father of Tiny Tim

characters.name: Fred
characters.notes: Cheerful nephew who invites Scrooge to Christmas dinner yearly

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Past
characters.notes: Childlike/old figure with light and extinguisher cap; shows Scrooge's history

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Present
characters.notes: Jolly giant in green robe with torch; shows current Christmas joy and want

characters.name: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
characters.notes: Silent shrouded figure; shows possible grim future

characters.name: Tiny Tim
characters.notes: Crippled youngest Cratchit; emblem of innocence and vulnerability

characters.name: Mrs. Cratchit
characters.notes: Bob's wife; proud, loving, resents Scrooge

characters.name: Belle
characters.notes: Released Scrooge from engagement when gold became his idol

characters.name: Mr. Fezziwig
characters.notes: Scrooge's generous former master who threw joyful Christmas parties

characters.name: Fan
characters.notes: Scrooge's kind younger sister; mother of Fred

characters.name: Portly gentlemen
characters.notes: Seek donations for the poor on Christmas Eve

characters.name: Old Joe
characters.notes: Fence/pawnbroker who buys scavenged goods of the dead man

characters.name: Mrs. Dilber
characters.notes: One of the scavengers selling the dead man's effects

locations_mentioned: London streets and court on Christmas Eve
country road and market-town of Scrooge's boyhood
Bob Cratchit's four-roomed house in Camden Town
obscure foul quarter of town / Old Joe's shop
dark bare room with uncurtained bed
timeline: Seven years after Marley's death (stated on Christmas Eve)
Christmas Eve afternoon/evening: counting-house, streets, Scrooge home alone
Night of Christmas Eve: Marley's Ghost visit; warning of three spirits
When the bell tolls One: Ghost of Christmas Past; visions of Scrooge's past Christmases
Next night same hour: Ghost of Christmas Present; Christmas Day scenes across London and beyond
When last stroke of Twelve ceases: Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come; future shadows
Christmas Day: turkey errand, church, streets, dinner at Fred's
Next morning (Boxing Day): office; raises Bob's salary
Thereafter: Scrooge keeps Christmas all year; Tiny Tim lives
withheld_name_or_twist_rules: Do not confirm Marley's Ghost identity or full purpose before B6-B7 (knocker first appears as face only)
Do not name or fully describe the three Spirits before their respective arrival beats (B8, B14, B20)
Do not reveal the dead man in future visions is Scrooge until the gravestone beat B25
Do not confirm Tiny Tim dies in the unaltered future until the Cratchit mourning scene; keep 'vacant seat' prophecy as warning
Do not show Scrooge's full reformation or Christmas morning joy before the bedpost transformation B26
Keep Ignorance and Want unnamed until the Spirit presents them near end of Present visit
Fred's party game identifying 'Uncle Scrooge' as the disagreeable animal should land as comic reveal inside that beat only

essential_beats.summary: Establish Marley is dead and Scrooge is a cold, covetous, solitary miser whom even dogs avoid; firm still bears both names.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Opening insists Marley is dead as a door-nail; Scrooge is squeezing grasping old sinner who ices his office and answers to both names.

essential_beats.summary: Christmas Eve in the counting-house: tiny fires, fog, Scrooge watches clerk; nephew Fred arrives wishing merry Christmas.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Cold bleak foggy afternoon; clerk in Tank tries to warm at candle; Fred bursts in glowing and greets uncle.

essential_beats.summary: Fred and Scrooge argue: Christmas is humbug vs kind forgiving time; Scrooge refuses dinner invitation and dismisses him.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Scrooge calls Christmas humbug and time for paying bills; Fred defends it as charitable; clerk applauds then snuffs fire; Scrooge says good afternoon repeatedly.

essential_beats.summary: Two portly charity gentlemen seek donation for poor; Scrooge refuses, cites prisons and workhouses, says surplus population should die.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Gentlemen present credentials; Scrooge asks about prisons, Union workhouses, Treadmill; wishes to be left alone; they withdraw.

essential_beats.summary: Closing time: Scrooge grudgingly allows clerk the day off; clerk slides on ice home; Scrooge dines alone and returns to gloomy chambers.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Scrooge complains of paying for no work; clerk races to Camden Town; Scrooge melancholy tavern then dark yard and rooms once Marley's.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge sees Marley's face in the door knocker; enters, double-locks, checks rooms, sits by low fire for gruel.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Knocker becomes Marley's face with spectacles; Scrooge startled but enters; searches sitting-room bedroom lumber-room; locks himself in.

essential_beats.summary: Bells ring; Marley's Ghost enters dragging cash-box chain; Scrooge doubts senses then believes; Marley explains he forged chain in life and must wander.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Disused bell swings then all bells; clanking up stairs; transparent Marley with ledgers padlocks; jaw drops; spirit within must walk or be condemned; chain made link by link.

essential_beats.summary: Marley warns three Spirits will come; shows Scrooge other fettered phantoms outside; vanishes; Scrooge falls asleep.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Expect first tomorrow when bell tolls One, second next night, third when Twelve ceases; window opens; air full of chained moaning ghosts; Scrooge to bed.

essential_beats.summary: Clock strikes One; Ghost of Christmas Past appears (child-old figure with holly and light-cap); takes Scrooge through wall to boyhood country road and lonely school.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Curtains drawn by hand; strange figure white tunic jet of light; Scrooge's past; open country snow; solitary child reading left at school; Scrooge weeps.

essential_beats.summary: Past vision: young Scrooge's sister Fan arrives to bring him home for Christmas; schoolmaster scene; then Fezziwig's warehouse Christmas Eve ball.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Little Fan kisses brother; father kinder; Fezziwig closes early, clears floor, fiddler, dances with Mrs Fezziwig, apprentices praise him; Scrooge defends Fezziwig's power to make happy.

essential_beats.summary: Past vision: older Scrooge with Belle who releases him because Gain has displaced her; later scene of Belle happily married with children.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Girl in mourning says golden idol displaced her; contract made when poor; she frees him; another room mother and daughter; husband mentions seeing solitary Scrooge; Scrooge begs no more.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge struggles with Past Spirit, forces extinguisher cap down; light still streams; he reels to bed exhausted.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Wrestles Ghost whose face holds fragments of all shown; presses cap; cannot hide light; sinks into heavy sleep in own bedroom.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge wakes to clock near One; prepares for second Spirit; finds own room transformed into green grove throne of food; Ghost of Christmas Present appears.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Touches curtains himself; ruddy light from next room; enters to holly berries blaze and heaped turkeys geese punch; jolly Giant with glowing torch invites him.

essential_beats.summary: Present Spirit takes Scrooge through joyful snowy Christmas morning streets, markets, bakers; sprinkles torch blessing especially on poor dinners.
essential_beats.source_evidence: People shovel snow laughing; poulterers fruiterers grocers radiant; churchgoers; poor carry dinners to bakers; Spirit's incense restores good humour; Scrooge questions Seventh Day closing.

essential_beats.summary: Visit to Cratchit home: poor but merry family prepares goose and pudding; Tiny Tim arrives on Bob's shoulder; family toasts; Spirit foretells Tim's death if future unaltered.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Mrs Cratchit ribbons; Martha hides then appears; Tiny Tim crutch iron frame; goose admired; pudding blazing; Bob proposes merry Christmas; Tim God bless us every one; vacant seat and crutch if shadows remain.

essential_beats.summary: Spirit shows Christmas among miners on moor, lighthouse keepers, and sailors at sea all keeping the day; then arrives at Fred's lively party.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Bleak moor hut singing; lighthouse two men grog song; ship every man kinder word; sudden hearty laugh is nephew's; bright room games music.

essential_beats.summary: At Fred's: guests mock Scrooge yet Fred pities and toasts him; games of blind-man's buff, forfeits, Yes and No (Scrooge is the animal); Scrooge joins unseen and softens.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Niece pretty; Topper chases plump sister; music recalls Fan; Yes and No identifies Uncle Scrooge; they drink his health anyway; Scrooge begs to stay.

essential_beats.summary: Spirit ages; from robe emerge two wretched children Ignorance and Want; Spirit warns beware especially the boy; echoes Scrooge's prisons/workhouses line as bell strikes twelve.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Hair grey; life ends tonight; claw-like foot; boy and girl yellow meagre wolfish; Doom on boy's brow; Are there no prisons? Spirit vanishes; Phantom approaches.

essential_beats.summary: Silent Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come appears; Scrooge vows to change and follows the shrouded pointing figure into the city.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Deep black garment only hand visible; Scrooge kneels in dread; asks if shadows of things that will be; Spirit points onward; Scrooge prepared with thankful heart.

essential_beats.summary: Future Exchange: businessmen discuss a dead man's cheap funeral with indifference and jokes; Scrooge sees no image of himself in his usual place.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Fat man and others: dead last night, what of money, cheap funeral volunteer if lunch; another pair 'Old Scratch has got his own'; Scrooge seeks his own likeness unsuccessfully.

essential_beats.summary: In foul quarter Old Joe's shop: charwoman, laundress, undertaker's man sell bed-curtains, blankets, shirt stripped from the corpse; they laugh that he frightened all away.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Grey-haired rascal; three enter with bundles; bed-curtains rings and all; blankets; best shirt taken off body; Ha ha end of it profit us when dead; Scrooge recoils in horror.

essential_beats.summary: Spirit shows bare plundered bed with covered body unwatched unwept; Scrooge cannot lift the cover; begs to see any emotion caused by the death.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Dark room pale light on bed; cat and rats; Scrooge thinks of avarice bringing rich end; asks for tenderness connected with a death.

essential_beats.summary: Only emotion shown is relief: young couple (Caroline) learn the merciless creditor is dead and may sleep with light hearts.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Mother anxious; husband returns; he is dead; she thankful then prays forgiveness; debt may transfer but successor unlikely so hard; happier house for this man's death.

essential_beats.summary: Cratchit house in mourning: Tiny Tim has died; Bob returns from churchyard visit; family gentle; Fred has been kind; they vow to remember Tim.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Quiet children; Peter reads scripture; mother sewing poor Tim's things; Bob walks slower; kisses little face upstairs; nephew offered help; Bob happy they will not quarrel remembering Tim.

essential_beats.summary: Spirit leads to churchyard; points to neglected grave; Scrooge reads his own name EBENEZER SCROOGE; begs to know if courses can change the ends; clutches hand and vows to honour Christmas.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Iron gate churchyard; wretched man lay here; Are these things that Will be or May be; stone bears his name; I am not the man I was; sponge away the writing; Spirit dwindles to bedpost.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge awakens in his own bed on Christmas morning; overjoyed curtains intact; laughs and cries; learns from boy it is Christmas Day; spirits did it all in one night.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Bedpost his own; Time before him to make amends; frisks; churches peal; open window clear cold bright; boy in Sunday clothes confirms Christmas Day; Scrooge giddy as schoolboy.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge sends boy to buy prize turkey for Cratchits anonymously; tips generously; dresses and walks streets delighting in greetings.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Big turkey as big as boy; cab to Camden Town; chuckles; shaves and best clothes; people wish merry Christmas; he answers blithely.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge finds the portly charity gentleman, apologises, and whispers a large donation including back-payments; invites him to visit.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Pang then takes both hands; merry Christmas; not a farthing less; gentleman astonished munificence; will come and see him.

essential_beats.summary: Scrooge goes to church then to Fred's; shyly enters and is welcomed heartily to dinner and party; wonderful happiness.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Passes door dozen times; asks girl; sidles in Fred!; niece starts; let him in shake arm off; wonderful party games unanimity.

essential_beats.summary: Next morning Scrooge arrives early, pretends anger at Bob's lateness, then leaps to raise his salary and help his family; becomes second father to Tiny Tim.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Eighteen and a half minutes late; growls step this way; dig in waistcoat then merry Christmas raise salary smoking bishop coal-scuttle; Tiny Tim did not die; good friend master man.

essential_beats.summary: Epilogue: Scrooge keeps Christmas all year thereafter; no more spirits; it was always said he knew how to keep Christmas well; God bless Us Every One.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Total Abstinence from spirits; some laughed at alteration he heeded little; own heart laughed; Tiny Tim's observation closes.
